question: Host discovery beyond the keyed list: apply the own-name (NP) rule to every recipient EIN with top-50 lines, flagging EINs that receive >= 3 distinct filed names sharing no non-generic token with the BMF or modal name; hand-check the top 30 candidate EINs by dollars for unlisted fiscal sponsors
conclusion_affected: Whether the de facto host set (11 EINs) and the $35.1m-$114.6m addition miss hosts that no filer names with FBO
rationale: This task restricted NP to the 347 keyed EINs, where it adds $0 because the EIN-keyed flag already counts every line; the only route by which NP can add dollars is discovery of hosts outside the list

question: Host-alias table from archived EO BMF names: for the 347 keyed EINs, collect every NAME seen in the NCCS monthly BMF archive 2022-2026 and add them to the reference names before applying the NP rule; re-measure NP precision
conclusion_affected: NP-rule precision (63% lines, 40% dollars in the sample) and the FBO-rule recall estimate
rationale: 22 of 60 sampled NP lines are host aliases or own programmes (King Baudouin Foundation US for Myriad USA, Trust for Conservation Innovation for Multiplier, Rainier Valley Corps for RVC Seattle, The Field, Mother Jones); an archived-name list removes most of them mechanically

question: Myriad USA (formerly King Baudouin Foundation United States) lines: read the 26 NP lines' purpose texts and Myriad's own Form 990 Schedule F to decide whether its $18.2m of top-50 inflows are foreign pass-through grants and belong to the foreign category rather than the fiscal-sponsor category
conclusion_affected: Category assignment of $18.2m (plus Myriad's other top-50 lines) between fiscal-sponsor and foreign flags
rationale: All 26 NP lines to EIN 58-2277856 are filed under the host's former name; one purpose text names a foreign beneficiary (American Friends of Soleterre, Turkey & Syria earthquake fund). Myriad is a directory host already counted in the refined flag

question: Parenthetical host names: extend the FBO-name detector with a rule for 'PROJECT (HOST)' names, which mission_exception_refined.name_key strips (e.g. 'Arab Resource ganizing Center (AROC) - 1073 (TIDES CENTER)', 'HOUSE OF VICTORY FOUNDATION (COMMUNITY INITIATIVES)'); report how many lines move from NP to the FBO rule
conclusion_affected: FBO-rule recall (about 56% of lines on keyed hosts)
rationale: Two NP lines name the host in parentheses; the FBO rule cannot see them because the parenthetical is removed before matching

question: Graduated projects: for NP lines whose project name matches another BMF entity, compare that entity's ruling month with the grant year to separate projects that later got their own exemption from filer EIN errors
conclusion_affected: Small; whether a few NP lines are misattributed EINs rather than sponsored projects
rationale: 13 NP lines ($0.39m) share a name key with another BMF EIN; in the sample, Arte Noir's own ruling (2022-12) predates the grant, while Skyway Coalition (2025-04) and Rod Dedeaux Foundation (2024-10) follow it
